inputs.need: Adults with refractory neuropathic pain in our hospital pain clinic are being offered intravenous ketamine infusions with no shared protocol. Doses range from 0.5 to 1 mg/kg/h, sessions last 4 to 6 hours, courses run from 1 to 5 days, and nobody follows outcomes past the next clinic visit. The infusion chairs and nursing time are scarce, and I am not sure the chairs are worth it. I want to know whether a randomized trial of a standard ketamine protocol is justified and feasible here, or whether something smaller should come first.
inputs.constraints: No external funding before mid-2027. Two infusion chairs, one day per week. Existing clinic nurses only. Outcomes must include function and not only pain scores.
localFacts: The pain clinic gave 212 ketamine infusion sessions to 58 patients between September 2025 and August 2026 (clinic infusion log).
Hospital pharmacy agreed on 2026-09-10 to prepare ketamine infusions in standard 250 mL bags (pharmacy memo PH-2026-091).
The research ethics board has not reviewed any ketamine protocol from this clinic.
